Born Arjumand Banu Begum and niece of the formidable Nur Jahan, this Mughal empress so moved her husband Shah Jahan that he built one of the Wonders of the World as her tomb — who was she?
Mumtaz Mahal: Empress of the Mughal Empire from 1628 to 1631.

Emerging after World War II, this far-right ideology borrows core elements from an earlier authoritarian movement while adding ultranationalism, racial supremacy and anti-immigrant sentiment — what is it?

In Hesiod's 'Theogony,' this Greek personification of night was said to be so powerful that even Zeus feared displeasing her, and she rode across the sky in a chariot pulled by horses. Who is this goddess?
Nyx: Ancient Greek goddess of the night. In ancient Greek art, Nyx often appears alongside other celestial deities such as Selene, Helios and Eos, as a winged figure driving a horse-pulled chariot.
Coined by French peace campaigner Émile Arnaud in 1901, this opposition to war and violence was embodied in Gandhi's philosophy of steadfast nonviolent resistance, 'satyagraha' — what is it?

Pacifism: Philosophy opposing war or violence. Its effectiveness served as inspiration to Martin Luther King Jr., James Lawson, James Bevel, Thích Nhất Hạnh, and many others in the civil rights movement.
Twice elected mayor of Washington D.C., this Whig newspaperman amassed one of the most extensive private collections of Revolutionary-era maps and manuscripts in America — who was he?
Peter Force: American politician and historian (1790–1868)
Who is this — “Greek god of fertility and male genitalia”?
Priapus: Greek god of fertility and male genitalia. Priapus is marked by his oversized penis, and his permanent erection, which gave rise to the medical term priapism.

Beginning and ending with the sighting of a crescent moon, this 29-to-30-day observance is one of Islam's five pillars and the month when the Quran is believed to have been first revealed — what is it?
Ramadan: Ninth month of the Islamic calendar and month-long fasting event in Islam.
Ukraine's wealthiest man, this businessman owns FC Shakhtar Donetsk and has funneled hundreds of millions of dollars in wartime aid through his foundation — who is he?
Rinat Akhmetov: Ukrainian businessman. Rinat Leonidovych Akhmetov (born 21 September 1966) is a Ukrainian oligarch, billionaire and businessman.
Beginning in February 2014 with Russia's annexation of Crimea and a war in the Donbas, this conflict escalated into Europe's biggest war since World War II — what is it called?
Russo-Ukrainian war: Ongoing conflict since 2014. It then supported Russian separatist armed groups who started a war in the eastern Donbas region against Ukraine's military.
Leader of Spain's far-right Vox party since 2014 and president of Patriots.eu since 2024, this politician represents Madrid in the Congress of Deputies — who is he?
Named after the TV show in which its founder played a fictional president, this Ukrainian political party has ruled since Volodymyr Zelenskyy won the presidency in 2019 — which party?
Servant of the People: Political party in Ukraine. It was formed in late 2017 and was officially registered on 31 March 2018 on the basis of the previously registered Party of Decisive Changes.
Ruling from 893 to 927, this monarch's campaigns against the Byzantines and Magyars brought the First Bulgarian Empire to its greatest size and a cultural Golden Age — who was he?
Simeon I of Bulgaria: First Emperor of the Bulgars from 893 to 927.
A Princeton grad and former F-15 flight test engineer, he co-founded the deep-sea firm OceanGate and died in 2023 when its submersible imploded en route to the Titanic wreck — who was he?
Described in its founding text as formless, eternal, and the 'Mother of the universe,' this East Asian philosophical concept's Chinese character means 'the way' or 'path' — what is it?
Tao: Philosophical concept native to China.

Named as a single people by the ancient Greeks, this Indo-European group inhabited modern Bulgaria, Romania, and parts of Greece and Turkey, giving rise to tribes like the Getae and Dacians — who were they?
Thracians: Indo-European people in ancient southeast Europe.

Proclaimed by the Central Council after the October Revolution and formally independent from Russia by January 1918, what short-lived Eastern European state emerged from the collapsing Russian Empire?
Ukrainian People's Republic: 1917–18/1918–21 state in Eastern Europe.
This Hungarian lawyer-politician has led the Fidesz party and served as prime minister twice, taking the country into NATO during his first stint. Who is he?
Viktor Orbán: Prime Minister of Hungary (1998–2002, 2010–2026)
This early American writer gave us 'Rip Van Winkle' and 'The Legend of Sleepy Hollow,' and later served as the U.S. ambassador to Spain — who was he?
Washington Irving: American writer, historian and diplomat (1783–1859)
The only Democrat elected president during the Republican-dominated Progressive Era, he steered the U.S. through World War I and championed the League of Nations — which 28th president was he?
Woodrow Wilson: President of the United States from 1913 to 1921.
A close associate of Gandhi and a founder of Jamia Millia Islamia, this Berlin-educated educationist rose to become president of India, dying in office in 1969 — who was he?
Zakir Husain: President of India from 1967 to 1969.
Which of these people was born first?
Benjamin Banneker (born 1731) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these people was born first?
Ellen Swallow Richards (born 1842) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four is the eldest?
Henry Vaughan (born 1621) is the earliest of the four. Henry Vaughan (1621 – 23 April 1695) was a Welsh metaphysical poet, author and translator writing in English, and a medical physician.
COBOL (founded 1959) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four appeared first?
Lisp (programming language) (published 1958) is the earliest of the four.
Pick the physicist from these four.
Mark Oliphant is a physicist. Born and raised in Adelaide, South Australia, Oliphant graduated from the University of Adelaide in 1922.
Who among these is a chemist?
Carolyn Bertozzi is a chemist. Carolyn Ruth Bertozzi (born October 10, 1966) is an American chemist and Nobel laureate, known for her wide-ranging work spanning both chemistry and biology.
What is the atomic number of Fluorine?
Fluorine is a chemical element; it has symbol F and atomic number 9.
In what year was Bernie Madoff born?
Bernie Madoff: Madoff's firm had two basic units: a stock brokerage and an asset management business; the Ponzi scheme was centered in the asset management business.
In what year was H. H. Holmes born?
H. H. Holmes: Holmes, was an American con artist and serial killer active between 1891 and 1894.
In what year was Alan Turing born?
Alan Turing: Alan Mathison Turing (23 June 1912 – 7 June 1954) was an English mathematician, computer scientist, logician, cryptanalyst, philosopher and theoretical biologist.
In what year did Émile Durkheim die?
Émile Durkheim: David Émile Durkheim (French: [emil dyʁkɛm] or [dyʁkajm]; 15 April 1858 – 15 November 1917) was a French sociologist.
In what year did Ferdinand Porsche die?
Ferdinand Porsche (3 September 1875 – 30 January 1951) was an Austrian-German automotive engineer and founder of the Porsche AG.
In what year was Citric acid discovered?
Citric acid is an organic compound with the formula C6H8O7.
In what year was Gold discovered?
Gold is a chemical element; its chemical symbol is Au (from Latin aurum) and atomic number 79.
Methylprednisolone: Pfizer. It is either used at low doses for chronic illnesses or used at high doses during acute flares.
In which country is Embraer E-Jet family based?
Embraer E-Jet family: Brazil. The E-Jet was designed to complement Embraer's earlier ERJ family, the company's first jet-powered regional aircraft.
Who is credited with discovering Tantalum?
Tantalum: Anders Gustaf Ekeberg. Tantalum is a chemical element; it has symbol Ta and atomic number 73.
Who is credited with discovering L'Hôpital's rule?
L'Hôpital's rule: Johann Bernoulli. The differentiation of the numerator and denominator often simplifies the quotient or converts it to a limit that can be directly evaluated by continuity.
Who is credited with discovering Sulfur?
Sulfur: Antoine Lavoisier. Sulfur (American spelling or sulphur (Commonwealth spelling) is a chemical element; it has symbol S and atomic number 16.
Formed by the angle of thyroid cartilage around the voice box, this neck protrusion becomes a prominent secondary sex characteristic in most men during puberty — what is it commonly called?
Adam's apple is the protrusion in the neck formed by the angle of the thyroid cartilage surrounding the larynx, typically visible in men and less so in women.
Ranging from South Florida to Peru, this reptile is the most widespread member of its family in the Americas and one of only two species that commonly thrive in saltwater — which species?
American crocodile (Crocodylus acutus) is a species of crocodilian found in the Neotropics.
Known as 'doodlebugs' for the trails they leave in sand, these insect larvae dig pits to ambush wandering ants, while the winged adults are often mistaken for dragonflies — what are they?
Antlion are a group of about 2,000 species of insect in the neuropteran family Myrmeleontidae.

The third-largest member of its family behind the Siberian taimen and Pacific Chinook, this anadromous fish hatches in rivers, matures at sea, and changes color and appearance when it returns upstream to spawn — name this fish?
Atlantic salmon (Salmo salar) is a species of ray-finned fish in the family Salmonidae.
This steroid medication treats conditions ranging from rheumatoid arthritis and psoriasis to asthma, and is also given before preterm birth to help speed a baby's lung development — what drug is it?
Betamethasone is a steroid medication. It can be taken by mouth, injected into a muscle, or applied to the skin, typically in cream, lotion, or liquid forms.
This incurable, always-fatal disease of cattle causes abnormal behavior and trouble walking, with symptoms that may take four to five years to appear after infection — what is this disorder called?
Bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE), commonly known as mad cow disease, is an incurable and always fatal neurodegenerative disease of cattle.
Sole living family in the mammalian suborder Tylopoda, which group unites camels with llamas and their South American relatives?
Camelidae is a family of mammals belonging to the ungulate order Artiodactyla (even-toed ungulates) and the only living family in the suborder Tylopoda.
This class of ribbon-like parasitic flatworms sheds egg-packed body segments called proglottids into the environment to infect new hosts — what is this class called (scientific name)?
Cestoda is a class of parasitic worms in the flatworm phylum (Platyhelminthes).
This anatomical term for the hollow between a woman's breasts was coined in its modern sense by a Hollywood censor reviewing the 1943 film starring Jane Russell — what is the term?
Cleavage (breasts) is the narrow depression or hollow between the breasts of a woman.
This group of related RNA viruses causes respiratory illnesses ranging from the mild common cold to deadly diseases like SARS, MERS, and COVID-19 — what's this virus family called?
Coronavirus are a group of related RNA viruses that cause diseases in mammals and birds.
Nicknamed for the material that made up most of its airframe, this British twin-engined combat aircraft of World War II was one of the fastest operational planes of 1941. What aircraft is this?
De Havilland Mosquito was a British twin-engined, multi-role combat aircraft, introduced during the Second World War.
This C-shaped first section of the small intestine connects the stomach to the jejunum and is the body's principal site for absorbing iron — what is it?
Duodenum is the first section of the small intestine in most vertebrates, including mammals, reptiles, and birds.
This Italian-American physicist won the 1938 Nobel Prize, built the world's first artificial nuclear reactor (Chicago Pile-1), and is called the "architect of the nuclear age" — who was he?

Enrico Fermi (29 September 1901 - 28 November 1954) was an Italian-American physicist, renowned for being the creator of the world's first artificial nuclear reactor, the Chicago Pile-1, and a member of the Manhattan Project.
Home to seven living cat species, from the tiny black-footed cat to the jungle cat, and the wild ancestor line of the housecat, which genus of felines is this?
Felis is a genus of small and medium-sized cat species native to most of Africa and south of 60 latitude in Europe and Asia to Indochina.
Most common in the hands and feet, this cold-exposure injury can lead to complications like hypothermia or compartment syndrome — what is it called?
Frostbite is an injury to skin or other living tissue that is allowed to freeze, especially affecting the fingers, toes, nose, ears, cheeks and chin.
This 1984 period drama imagines a bitter rivalry between an 18th-century Vienna composer and his jealous rival, who resolves to ruin the genius's career. What film is it?
Glyphosate (IUPAC name: N-(phosphonomethyl)glycine) is a broad-spectrum systemic herbicide and crop desiccant.
Hailed by Time as a 2019 'Pioneer' yet condemned as a mad scientist, which Chinese biophysicist announced in 2018 that he'd created the first gene-edited human babies?
He Jiankui (pinyin: H Jinku HUH KWAY; born 1984) is a Chinese biophysicist known for his controversial first use of genome editing in humans in 2018.
One of the six Celtic nations, this peninsula in northwest France was known as Armorica under Roman rule before becoming an independent kingdom and later a duchy. What region is it?
Hydra (genus) is a genus of small freshwater hydrozoans in the phylum Cnidaria.
An ISO standard defines it as "a new or changed entity, realizing or redistributing value" — and it's related to, but not the same as, invention. What word are we after?
Innovation is the practical implementation of ideas that result in the creation or improvements of goods or services.

Called 'the greatest investor on Wall Street,' this founder of Renaissance Technologies made his fortune using mathematical models, after co-developing a key concept in differential geometry — who is he?
Jim Simons (April 25, 1938 - May 10, 2024) was an American hedge fund manager, investor, mathematician, and philanthropist.
Her women's absolute land speed record stood until 2019, she got her own action figure, and Google honored her with a Doodle in 2023 — this deaf stuntwoman and racer. Who is she?
Kitty O'Neil ((1946-03-24)March 24, 1946 - (2018-11-02)November 2, 2018) was an American stuntwoman and auto-racer, often called "the fastest woman in the world" for her various speed records.
This American computer scientist rose to prominence after Elon Musk praised his MIT study on Tesla's semi-autonomous driving system, and now hosts a long-form interview podcast. Who is he?
Lex Fridman (born 15 August 1983) is an American computer scientist and podcaster.
Enclosed in a fibrous capsule and linked throughout the body by lymphatic vessels, these kidney-shaped organs filter foreign particles and house the immune system's B and T cells — what are they?
Lymph node is a kidney-shaped organ of the lymphatic system and the adaptive immune system.
Number theory, algebra, geometry, analysis and set theory are all branches of this field, which leans on logical reasoning and proof to study abstract concepts — what is it?
Mathematics is a field of knowledge concerned with abstract concepts such as numbers, geometric shapes, sets, functions, and probabilities.
Carrying the NATO reporting name 'Halo,' this Soviet/Russian heavy transport helicopter is the largest of its kind ever to enter serial production — name the aircraft?
Mil Mi-26 is a Soviet/Russian heavy transport helicopter.
Likened to insulation on an electrical wire, this fatty material sheaths axon segments to speed up the transmission of nerve impulses — what is it called?

Myelin is a lipid-rich material that in most vertebrates surrounds the axons of neurons to insulate them and increase the rate at which electrical impulses (called action potentials) pass along the axon.

Born in New York to Jewish Holocaust-survivor parents, this Princeton-trained political scientist studies the politics of the Holocaust and the Israeli–Palestinian conflict — and his 2007 DePaul tenure fight made headlines. Who is he?
Norman Finkelstein (born December 8, 1953) is an American political scientist and activist.

This female reproductive gland produces eggs that travel through the oviduct to the uterus, while also functioning as an endocrine organ that secretes hormones governing the menstrual cycle — what organ is it?
Ovary (from Latin vrium 'egg') is a gonad in the female reproductive system that produces ova; when released, an ovum travels through the oviduct into the uterus.
It comes in a G version for the needle and a V version for the mouth, and it owes its name to the very mould it's coaxed from — which medication?
Penicillin (PCN or PEN) are a group of beta-lactam antibiotics originally obtained from Penicillium moulds, principally P. chrysogenum.
Native to South America and the most economically important member of the Bromeliaceae family, this tropical 'multiple fruit' became a 17th-century European symbol of luxury — what is it?
Pineapple (Ananas comosus) is a tropical plant with an edible fruit; it is the most economically significant plant in the family Bromeliaceae.

Native to North American grasslands, these burrowing, herbivorous ground squirrels come in five species, black-tailed, white-tailed, Gunnison's, Utah, and Mexican. Name this genus, Cynomys, by its common two-word name?
Prairie dog (genus Cynomys) are herbivorous burrowing ground squirrels native to the grasslands of North America.
This white, odorless nitroamine explosive, widely used since World War II, is the explosive agent inside C-4 plastic explosive — what is it called?
RDX (Research Department Explosive or Royal Demolition Explosive), or hexogen, also known by other names, is an organic compound with the formula (CH2N2O2)3.
A Jesuit priest, poet, and diplomat from the Republic of Ragusa, this polymath produced an early precursor of atomic theory and in 1753 discovered the Moon has no atmosphere — who was he?
Roger Joseph Boscovich (18 May 1711 - 13 February 1787) was a physicist, astronomer, mathematician, philosopher, diplomat, poet, theologian, Jesuit priest, and a polymath from the Republic of Ragusa.
Found on every continent but Antarctica and numbering over 2,500 species, this eight-legged arachnid curves a stinger-tipped tail over its back — what is it?

Scorpion (order Scorpiones) are predatory arachnids with eight legs, a pair of grasping pincers (or Chelae) and a narrow, segmented tail, often carried in a characteristic forward curve over the back and always ending with a stinger.
This structural framework supporting an animal's body comes in three main forms — a rigid outer shell, a rigid inner frame, or a flexible fluid-supported structure — what is it called?
Skeleton is the structural frame that supports the body of most animals.
Also known as sea stars, roughly 1,900 species of these star-shaped marine invertebrates live on seabeds from warm tropics to icy polar oceans. What are they?
Starfish are a class of marine invertebrates generally shaped like a star polygon.
Appointed a government economic minister in 1991, this academic rose to become prime minister of Turkey in 1993 and later served as its foreign minister — who is she?
Tansu Çiller (born 24 May 1946) is a Turkish academic, economist, and politician who served as the 22nd prime minister of Turkey from 1993 to 1996.
A parasitic arachnid roughly 3 to 5 millimeters long that feeds on the blood of mammals and birds, with fossils dating back some 100 million years to the Cretaceous — which creature?
Tick are parasitic arachnids of the order Ixodida.
This break in the skin or mucous membrane involves tissue breakdown severe enough to expose the dermis or fat beneath, and often becomes infected with pus — what condition is it?
Ulcer (dermatology) is a sore on the skin or a mucous membrane, accompanied by the disintegration of tissue.
This slender, short-legged predator's genus also includes polecats, stoats, and ferrets, and its smallest species is the tiniest carnivore on Earth — what animal is it?
Weasel are mammals of the genus Mustela of the family Mustelidae.
Earning his doctorate in Islamic philosophy at George Washington University under Seyyed Hossein Nasr, this Turkish academic now directs the country's National Intelligence Organization — who is he?
İbrahim Kalın (born 15 September 1971) is a Turkish bureaucrat and academic who is the current director of the National Intelligence Organization (MT).
Considered sacred by Hindus and Buddhists, this tree native to the Indian subcontinent is also known as bael and is the sole member of its genus — which species?
Aegle marmelos: Species of tree, considered sacred by Hindus. It is present in India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, and Nepal as a naturalized species.

An anatomist and archaeologist turned TV presenter, she has served as professor of Public Engagement in Science at the University of Birmingham since 2012 and once led the charity Humanists UK — who is she?
Alice Roberts: English academic, TV presenter and author.
Nominated by Donald Trump in 2020, this Notre Dame law professor became the fifth woman to serve as a US Supreme Court associate justice after previously sitting on the Seventh Circuit — who is she?

Amy Coney Barrett: US Supreme Court justice since 2020. Barrett graduated from Rhodes College before attending Notre Dame Law School, earning a Juris Doctor (J.D.) degree in 1997 and ranked first in her class.
This external body opening at the end of the digestive tract, positioned opposite the mouth, lets gas and solid waste pass out after digestion?
Anus: Digestive tract waste expulsion opening. Passage of feces through the anus is typically controlled by muscular sphincters, and failure to stop unwanted passages results in fecal incontinence.
Ranking as the second-largest lizard species after the Komodo dragon, this excellent swimmer thrives in lakes, rivers, and even city sewers across South and Southeast Asia — what is it?
Asian water monitor: Species of lizard. The Asian water monitor (Varanus salvator) is a large varanid lizard native to South and Southeast Asia.
As the largest member of the grass family, one species of this plant can grow stalks over 46 meters tall and 36 centimeters thick — name the plant?
Bamboo: Subfamily of plants in the grass family.
According to scholar John Carter, this discipline has two senses: a list of works consulted by an author, and the systematic study of books as physical objects — what's it called?
Bibliography: Organized listing of books and the systematic description of them as objects.
Built to replace the AH-1 Cobra, this twin-turboshaft attack helicopter packs a nose-mounted 30 mm chain gun and Hellfire missiles, with a two-person tandem cockpit — which aircraft is it?

Boeing AH-64 Apache: U.S. attack helicopter. The Apache began as the Model 77 developed by Hughes Helicopters for the United States Army's Advanced Attack Helicopter program to replace the AH-1 Cobra.

Native to Europe, West Asia, and parts of North Africa, this widely introduced game fish is one of the world's worst invasive species outside its home range, with regional names like sewin in Wales and finnock in Scotland — which species is it?
Brown trout: Species of fish. Brown trout are highly adaptable and have evolved numerous ecotypes/subspecies.

Derived from an East Asian evergreen tree's wood, this waxy, strong-smelling terpenoid can also be synthesized from oil of turpentine and occurs in small amounts in rosemary leaves. What compound is it?
An obligate carnivore with retractable claws and crepuscular hunting habits, this small domesticated mammal communicates with everything from purrs and trills to hisses — what is it?
Cat: Small domesticated carnivorous mammal. The cat (Felis catus), also called domestic cat and house cat, is a small domesticated carnivorous mammal.
Nicknamed 'Vigorous Dragon' and known to NATO as the Firebird, this Chinese delta-wing, canard-design fighter jet has been exported to Pakistan's air force — which aircraft, capable of Mach 1.8?
Chengdu J-10: Chinese multi-role fighter aircraft family.
Named after the French missionary who propagated it in Algeria, this citrus hybrid of mandarin and sweet orange is often sold as an 'Easy-peeler' — which fruit?
Clementine: Hybrid citrus fruit. The exterior is a deep orange colour with a smooth, glossy appearance.

Nocturnal and marked with narrow white crossbands on a bluish-black body, this South Asian snake's potent neurotoxic venom places it among the region's 'Big Four' most dangerous species — which snake?
Common krait: Species of snake. The common krait (Bungarus caeruleus) is a highly venomous snake species belonging to the genus Bungarus in the family Elapidae.
Nicknamed the mosquito hawk, which long-legged insect of the superfamily Tipuloidea is often mistaken for an oversized mosquito?
Crane fly: Superfamily of flies. The larvae of crane flies are known commonly as leatherjackets.
First created in 1994 and named for the German city where it was made, this synthetic element sits below platinum in group 10 — what is it?
Darmstadtium: Chemical element with atomic number 110 (Ds)
Produced by the enzyme 5α-reductase acting on a more familiar male sex hormone, this compound is a more potent driver of prostate growth, sebum, and body hair — which hormone?
Sometimes called 'word blindness,' this learning disability makes it hard to spell, sound out words, and read quickly, and often co-occurs with ADHD — what is it?

Often tangled up with mood, temperament, and creativity, these neurophysiological states carry a degree of pleasure or displeasure — yet scientists still can't agree on a single definition. What are they?
Dubbed the 'father of geometry,' this ancient Greek mathematician's treatise Elements dominated the field for nearly two thousand years — who is he?
This membranous bodily structure comes in superficial, visceral, and deep types, and a dangerous pressure buildup within it can cause compartment syndrome — what is it called?
Fascia: Layer of connective tissue in the body.
Sold under the brand name Prozac, this SSRI treats depression, OCD and panic disorder, and is also prescribed off-label for premature ejaculation — what is it?
Fluoxetine: SSRI antidepressant. It is also approved for treatment of major depressive disorder in adolescents and children 8 years of age and over.
Tucked beneath the liver, this pear-shaped organ stores and concentrates bile before releasing it to aid fat digestion in the small intestine — which organ?
Gallbladder: Organ in humans and other vertebrates.
Despite centuries of use in Korean and Chinese traditional medicine, no clinical evidence supports health claims for this Panax-genus root, often sold as a dietary supplement — what is it?
Ginseng: Root of a plant used in herbal preparations.
This junctional area between the torso and thigh, where the lower abdominal wall meets the leg, is commonly strained in a familiar sports injury — what is it called?
Groin: Area between the torso and the thigh. In human anatomy, the groin, also known as the inguinal region or iliac region, is the junctional area between the torso and the thigh.
This wingless insect spends its entire life on the human scalp, sipping blood, and can neither fly nor jump — its short stumpy legs can't even walk well on a flat surface. What tiny freeloader is it?
Head louse: Insect parasite of humans.
This academic discipline studies the methods, sources, and interpretive approaches historians use when writing about the past — what's it called?
Historiography: Study of the methods used by historians.
A yellow-flowered perennial whose leaves look perforated by translucent glands, this plant is famed in folklore and traditional medicine under a saintly common name — what is its botanical name?
Hypericum perforatum: Flowering plant in the St John's wort family.
Endemic to semiarid central-eastern Australia and also called the "fierce snake," this elapid was rediscovered in 1972 after nearly 90 years of obscurity — what is it?
Inland taipan: Extremely venomous snake native to Australia.

This Dutch microscopist showed that an insect's egg, larva, pupa, and adult are all one animal, pioneered the microscope in dissections, and in 1658 became the first to observe red blood cells — who was he?
Jan Swammerdam: Dutch biologist and microscopist (1637–1680)
Equal to the work done when a one-newton force moves an object one metre, this SI unit of energy is named for a 19th-century English physicist — which unit?
Joule: SI unit of energy. The joule ( JOOL, or JOWL; symbol: J) is the unit of energy in the International System of Units (SI).
Living as a recluse in a log house outside Kaluga, this Russian pioneer of rocket science inspired both Wernher von Braun and the architects of the Soviet space program — who is he?

Native to the dry grasslands and deserts of Afghanistan, Iran, Pakistan, India, and Nepal, this ground-dwelling reptile is so widely captive-bred it's considered the first domesticated species of its kind — what is it?
Leopard gecko: Species of reptile. The leopard gecko is a popular pet, and due to extensive captive breeding it is sometimes referred to as the first domesticated species of lizard.

This American stealth strike fighter comes in three flavors — conventional, short-takeoff/vertical-landing, and carrier-based — and with 883 in service is the world's fourth-most-numerous military aircraft. What is it?

Lockheed Martin F-35 Lightning II: American stealth multirole fighter aircraft. The Lockheed Martin F-35 Lightning II is an American family of single-seat, single-engine, supersonic stealth strike fighters.
With the formula MgCl2, this colorless salt forms hydrates and serves as the principal precursor to large-scale production of its namesake metal — what is it?
Magnesium chloride: Inorganic salt: MgCl2 and its hydrates. It forms hydrates MgCl2·nH2O, where n can range from 1 to 12.
Part of the chamomile tribe within the sunflower family, some species in this plant genus share the common name 'mayweed' — which genus?
Discovered in 1893 and existing as two mirror-image enantiomers, this CNS stimulant is best known in its hydrochloride-salt form nicknamed 'crystal' — what is it?
Medically termed a 'spontaneous abortion,' this is the loss of an embryo or fetus before it can survive independently — distinct from a stillbirth, which occurs after 20 weeks. What is it?
Miscarriage: Natural premature termination of pregnancy.

Made of contractile proteins called actin and myosin, this soft tissue exists in three vertebrate forms — skeletal, cardiac, and smooth — and forms during a developmental process called myogenesis — what is it?
Muscle: Important Biological tissue that allows movement.
Named after a German physical chemist, this electrochemistry formula calculates a reaction's reduction potential from temperature, electron count, and reactant concentrations — which relationship?
Nernst equation: Physical law in electrochemistry.
Built from a nitrogen-containing base, a five-carbon sugar, and a phosphate group, these molecules are the monomer building blocks of DNA and RNA — what are they called?
Nucleotide: Biological molecules constituting nucleic acids.

Believed to be the world's fourth-leading cause of disability, this degenerative joint disease comes from the breakdown of cartilage and bone, often striking the fingertips, thumb base, knees, and hips — what is it?
Osteoarthritis: Form of arthritis caused by degeneration of joints.
Known as the passion flower, this genus of about 550 species also has ornamental hybrids that have won Royal Horticultural Society awards and varieties used in ayahuasca analogs — name the genus?
Passiflora: Genus of flowering plants in the passion flower family.
Called the 'father of transplantation,' this Brazilian-born biologist won a 1960 Nobel for his work on acquired immune tolerance and graft rejection — who was he?
This imperial and US customary unit of volume is exactly one-eighth of a gallon, though the British version is about 20% larger than its American counterpart — which unit?

Pint: Unit of volume in the imperial and US systems. The pint (symbol pt, sometimes abbreviated as p) is a unit of volume or capacity in both the imperial and United States customary measurement systems.
Also called caustic potash and written KOH, this dangerously corrosive white solid is a prototypical strong base and the key precursor to most liquid and soft soaps — which compound?
Potassium hydroxide: Inorganic compound (KOH). It has many industrial and niche applications, most of which utilize its caustic nature and its reactivity toward acids.

This deep-sea fish off Australia and New Zealand has almost no muscle and a gelatinous body just under water's density, letting it float effortlessly at depths beyond 600 meters — what is its scientific name?
